reflection.text:
As Scientist on this run, my final call of Kinase inhibitors (p=0.48) was marked correct and matches the unblinded protocol truth (Kinase inhibitors) and protocol NSC vote. The unblinding is bryostatin CID 6435419 with name and BBBC021 structure agreement and ChEMBL mechanisms none curated (e17/e18), so there was no chemogenomic anchor - the call had to come from morphology.

What the evidence got right:

Acquisition strategy e1-e5 covered 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10 uM in rep 1. This span was decisive. Low dose e2: 679 cells, act_glcm_contrast z=-4.1 smoothed actin, cell_eccentricity +2.8 and nuc_eccentricity -2.7 - minimal phenotype. Mid dose e3: 715 cells, nuc_dna_mean z=-5.2 dilution plus nuc_solidity +2.8, nuc_eccentricity -2.8. Higher dose e4: 420 cells, nuc_dna_mean z=-7.8, nuc_eccentricity -7.6, cell_solidity -5.2 with cell count drop. High dose e5: 249 cells, act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std +16.3, tub_glcm_contrast +10.6 with severe loss. The monotonic nuc_dna_mean dilution rho=-1.00 p=0 over 4 doses (e9) and the 679->715->420->249 cell loss trend correctly signaled a dose-dependent polyploid/large-pale-nuclei phenotype rather than a single-well artifact, and e10 frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 and e12 cell_area rho=+0.80, though p=0.2, were consistent with that.

Atlas comparison e8 was the key that calibrated the call: NSC vote 3/4 Kinase inhibitors and k-neighbours Kinase inhibitors 4/10 vs DNA damage 2/10, Protein degradation 2/10. Per-well protocol details confirm this: 0.01 uM similarity 0.397, 0.1 uM 0.413, 1.0 uM 0.485 all nearest Kinase inhibitors, only the 10 uM well flipped to Microtubule stabilizers at 0.537 (tally 3 votes summed 1.295 vs 1 vote 0.537). I correctly weighted the three lower doses over the extreme high dose for the final hypothesis update e15-e16, rather than chasing the high-dose texture spike.

What misled / what I missed:

1. Aurora-like morphology strongly mimicked the truth class. Microscopist e6 (4 fields, density lower) called Aurora kinase inhibitors with 7 observations, and e4 nuc_eccentricity -7.6 + cell_solidity -5.2 + nuc_dna_mean -7.8 is textbook Aurora cytokinesis-failure/giant-cell. I retained Aurora at 0.22 in e15 for this reason. My e20 literature search 'kinase inhibitor polyploidy giant cell cytokinesis failure phenotype' returned 0 hits, so I had no literature to resolve broad Kinase inhibitors vs Aurora kinase inhibitors and had to rely on e8, which gave no Aurora support. Probability 0.48 correctly reflects that unresolved conflict.

2. High-dose actin/tubulin crisis misdirection. e5 extreme actin texture (+29.0) and tub_glcm_contrast +10.6 plus tub_mean rho=+0.80 (e14) and act_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 (e11) pushed Actin disruptors to 0.15 and Microtubule stabilizers to 0.08 in e15, and microscopist e7 (2 fields) called Actin disruptors. This was secondary toxicity, not primary MOA: it occurred only at 10 uM where cell count halved to 249 and was contradicted by the retention of tubulin signal at lower doses and by e8. I did not acquire the 4 unacquired doses or any replicate 2, so I could not test if e11 rho=+1.00 is truly monotonic or biphasic (-4.1 at low dose vs +29 at high dose) and I cited p=0.2 trends as supporting when they were non-significant.

3. Compound identity nuance. Literature e19/e21 shows bryostatin is classically described as an activator of protein kinase C PMID 3621472, PMID 2451575, with PKC and NF-kB-dependent mechanisms PMID 26199173 and PKC-dependent effects PMID 32437156, and work on PKC activator-induced phenotypes PMID 9770354. In ChEMBL there is no curated kinase inhibitor annotation (e17), but the atlas taxonomy bins this functional PKC modulation under Kinase inhibitors. My searches did not retrieve a paper directly linking bryostatin to the observed nuc_dna_mean dilution/polyploid phenotype, so I leaned on the protocol vote rather than a literature bridge.

In retrospect, the correct lesson is: trust the 3/4 NSC consensus across the non-toxic dose range and the dose-dependent DNA dilution, treat the 10 uM act/tub texture explosion as high-dose toxicity with cell loss, and keep Aurora as the main confuser. Acquisitions limited to rep 1 left budget exhausted with no replication; next time I would fill intermediate doses and a second replicate plus orthogonal DNA content/phospho-histone H3 to separate broad kinase/PKC effects from Aurora-specific failure, as noted in e16 rationale. No further free analysis would have overturned the decisive protocol vote noted in the review.

Acquisitions limited to rep 1 left budget exhausted with no replication; next time I would fill intermediate doses and a second replicate plus orthogonal DNA content/phospho-histone H3 to separate broad kinase/PKC effects from Aurora-specific failure, as noted in e16 rationale. No further free analysis would have overturned the decisive protocol vote noted in the review.

What was right:
- NSC 3/4 Kinase inhibitors e8 with summed similarity 1.295 vs 0.537, confirmed per-well 0.01-1 uM similarities 0.397/0.413/0.485
- monotonic nuc_dna_mean rho=-1.00 p=0 e9 plus cell count 679->715->420->249 tracking polyploid large-pale nuclei e3/e4
- downweighting high-dose actin/tubulin spike e5 z=+29.0/+10.6 and e7 actin call because e8 gave no support and tubulin retained

What was wrong or missed:
- Aurora kinase inhibitors retained at 0.22 due to e6 microscopist call and e4 nuc_eccentricity -7.6/cell_solidity -5.2 indistinguishable from Aurora giant-cell phenotype
- Actin disruptors/Microtubule stabilizers inflated by e5 extreme texture and e11 rho=+1.00/e13/e14 trends despite occurring only at toxic 10 uM with halved cell number
- reliance on p=0.2 trends e10 frac_large_nucleus +0.80 and e12 cell_area +0.80 as support without significance; no replicate 2 or intermediate doses acquired from e1 8-dose plate

Proposed next experiment: Not clinical advice. For screening follow-up: 8-point dose response with rep 2 including DMSO and reference kinase inhibitor control, plus flow cytometry DNA content and phospho-H3 to quantify polyploidy vs mitotic arrest, to distinguish broad kinase/PKC modulation from Aurora-specific cytokinesis failure.
